subject: MosaicHealth escalation — incident summary, targeted mitigations & exec alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Elliot <j.elliot@mosaichealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Ramos <aisha.ramos@mosaichealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production impact — elevated latency + 5xx spike across inference path

Mina,

We observed sustained latency surges and a sharp increase in 5xx errors from ~03:20 UTC on 2026-09-10. Impact: user requests to our patient search feature saw 3–5x latency, and approx 8% of requests returned server errors for a ~2 hour window. We rolled traffic to a fallback model but are still concerned about recurrence.

We captured short traces and sample request ids (attached: support-logs.txt). Our SRE flagged a correlation with increased batched requests hitting a particular model variant. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (deploys, kernel updates, autoscaler config) around that time?

This is affecting our operations; we'd like an incident bridge today and an RCA in writing within 72 hours. Please advise who on your side will own the investigation and when we can align on an executive readout.

Jordan
Jordan Elliot
Head of Platform Reliability, Mosaic Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Elliot <j.elliot@mosaichealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Ramos <aisha.ramos@mosaichealth.com>, david_kim@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — elevated latency + 5xx spike across inference path

Jordan — thanks for the alert and the logs. I’m sorry you hit this. I’ve looped in our on-call ops and platform leads (David, Kimberly) and we’ll take ownership of the investigation.

Immediate next steps:
- We’ll stand a short bridge at 14:00 PDT (21:00 UTC) today to triage — please confirm if that works for your SREs.
- I’ll share a readout and initial findings by EOD tomorrow (72-hour formal RCA will follow, we plan to deliver the first draft within 48–72 hours).
- Owners: David (kernel/runtime tracing + batching), Kimberly (autoscaler & deployment config), Neha (customer communication & exec sync).

I’ve attached the support logs you sent and we’ll capture additional traces.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: MosaicHealth outage triage — assignments and immediate asks

Team — escalation from MosaicHealth (external). Summary: latency 3–5x, 5xx ~8% for ~2 hours; customer routed to fallback model but wants RCA + exec readout. Bridge at 14:00 PDT.

Action items before bridge:
- David: collect kernel metrics, model variant logs, and KV-cache hit/miss counts for the timeframe (03:00–05:30 UTC). Prioritize traces for request ids in support-logs.txt.
- Kimberly: confirm recent autoscaler policy changes for the affected pool, recent deploys, and any burst-handling overrides. Pull cluster autoscaler and GPU utilization charts.
- Neha: prepare a short timeline template for the customer and draft the initial comms for execs (one-pager w/impact, timeline, mitigations).

Notes: customer traffic pattern indicates large prefix bursts and many padded requests — could be triggering quantized-kernel code paths under specific batch sizes. If we see a kernel regression, we may need a rolling rollback.

Attach: support-logs.txt (from customer).

— Mina

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Elliot <j.elliot@mosaichealth.com>, Aisha Ramos <aisha.ramos@mosaichealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: MosaicHealth — draft RCA & remediation plan (attached)

Jordan / Aisha — thank you for joining the bridge earlier. Attached is our draft RCA (mosaic_rca_draft_v1.pdf) and a kernel/prefix timeline (prefix_kv_timeline.csv). Summary of findings and planned mitigations below — this is a working draft and we welcome any corrections before the exec readout.

Executive summary (short):
- Root cause (primary): an interaction between a recent quantized-kernel optimization (deployed 2026-09-09) and a sudden shift in request-size distribution for your traffic (large prefix batches). Under certain batch-size alignments the quantized kernel path had increased lock contention and slower KV-cache population, leading to higher p99 latency and increased transient 5xx errors as requests timed out.
- Secondary contributor: an autoscaler policy that favored minimal GPU churn to reduce cost; during the surge the pool didn’t scale aggressively enough to absorb bursty batched traffic.

What we did (immediate mitigations):
1) Rolled back the quantized-kernel change for the affected model variant (completed 2026-09-10 05:30 UTC) — resolved the p95/p99 increase.
2) Temporarily adjusted autoscaler thresholds to allow faster scale-up for the Mosaic pool during burst windows.
3) Enabled additional KV-cache prefetching for your traffic pattern.

Planned corrective actions (next 30 days):
- Hotfix: kernel micro-patch to reduce lock contention for the quantized path (owner: David; target: 2026-09-17).
- Autoscaler tuning: a custom policy for MosaicHealth with burst-aware thresholds + manual playbook (owner: Kimberly; target: 2026-09-20).
- Quality validation: extended pre-prod load test with your request profile to validate batching/quantization interactions (owner: Platform Integrations; target: 2026-09-24).
- Post-deployment observation: 72-hour enhanced monitoring with daily check-ins and a rollback contingency plan.

Request for exec alignment: you requested an exec readout — we propose Tue 2026-09-14 10:00 PDT. We’ll present the RCA, action plan, and proposed SLA credit calculation. Please confirm attendees.

Attached: mosaic_rca_draft_v1.pdf, prefix_kv_timeline.csv

— Mina

From: Jordan Elliot <j.elliot@mosaichealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Ramos <aisha.ramos@mosaichealth.com>, platform-ops@mosaichealth.com
Date: 2026-09-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MosaicHealth — draft RCA & remediation plan (attached)

Thanks, Mina. The draft looks thorough and aligns with what our SREs saw. A few asks before the exec readout:

- Formal SLA credit request pathway and timeline (we’ll need the calculation and a point of contact).
- Can you commit to a hotfix timeline with a confirmed canary window?
- We’d like an assurance that model-variant rollouts won’t hit prod without a canary that simulates our prefix-heavy pattern.

We can make the Tue 9/14 10:00 PDT readout. Attendees from Mosaic: Jordan (Platform Reliability), Aisha (SRE), Chris Long (CISO). Expecting your exec + engineering leads.

Jordan

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: MosaicHealth — sprint kickoff and ownership (post-readout)

Team — exec readout completed with Mosaic earlier today. Summary: they accepted the RCA and want the hotfix and autoscaler tuning on the fast path; they also requested the SLA credit calc and a 72-hour observation period post-patch.

Confirmed owners and immediate commitments:
- David: complete kernel micro-patch and run canary against a synthetic prefix-heavy load — canary window Fri 2026-09-17 02:00–06:00 UTC. Deliverable: patch + canary report.
- Kimberly: implement custom burst-aware autoscaler policy for Mosaic pool and document manual playbook for emergency scale-up (deliverable: policy + playbook by 2026-09-20).
- Neha: own customer comms and SLA credit calc, coordinate legal for the credit pathway; deliverable: SLA memo & point-of-contact by 2026-09-16.

I’ve created ticket SUP-2345 for the hotfix and will update the HubSpot deal. We’ll cadence daily standups (15 min) until the 72-hour observation window completes.

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2345 — owners added.

— Mina
